THE GOLDEN'S OWN MESSAGE NAMES YOUR SITUATION, and it was written for a different campaign doing the same kind of work: "a cache changes WHEN a search runs, never WHAT it returns; a diff here means some change altered what a creature FEELS, not just how fast, and needs investigation before acceptance."

WHY I THINK IT APPLIES RATHER THAN JUST QUOTING IT. Your diff adds roughly 19 cache-shaped lines to windows/vessel/src/liveness.rs — cache/memo/reuse/BTreeMap/lazy — and touches essentially nothing matching arousal, valence, drive, arbitration, urgency or salience. So you changed WHEN things are computed and not WHAT they compute, and the seed-42 creature's arousal moved 0.735 -> 0.493 and its object of attention moved Thirst -> Danger. A value-preserving memo cannot do that. Same byte count, different bytes: this is a semantic change wearing a performance change's clothes.

THE OTHER TWO ARE THE SAME EVENT SEEN FROM DIFFERENT ANGLES, which is what makes me confident it is one cause rather than three:
  - the stranded creature now RECOVERS (recovery_ticks 4.0, chronicity 0.0) where it was chronically stuck. Its by_cause is entirely thirst, and thirst is exactly the drive the affect trace stopped attending to.
  - the co-location test reads "0 < 0". Both sides are ZERO — the healing effect did not shrink, it VANISHED. A comparison where both operands are zero is the signature of a measurement that has gone inert rather than one that moved.

WHAT I WOULD DO, IN THIS ORDER:
  1. Find why the memo is not value-preserving. The likeliest shapes: a key that omits something the value depends on, so a stale entry is served across a state change; or an insertion order that makes a tie-break order-dependent. Both produce exactly "same size, different values, different winner".
  2. Only once you understand it, decide whether the new behaviour is CORRECT. If the old chronic-stuck scoring was wrong and your change fixes it, that is a legitimate re-pin of all three -- but it is a world-behaviour decision that belongs in your ledger and probably a decision record, not a `make rebaseline-goldens`.
  3. `REBASELINE=1` will happily accept the new bytes and turn all three green. That is the one move that would make this invisible.

I have not read your implementation, so the mechanism above is the SHAPE the evidence fits, not a diagnosis. The three failures and their arithmetic are measured; the cause is yours to find.
